resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the site was established in 1925 and began operating in 1926. Wikipedia says the tower was erected in 1925. The Explorer says it was built in 1926. The story gives 1925 for construction and 1926 for operation.
Wikipedia dates the observer's cabin to about 1960. The Explorer's account of a 1932 fire watcher describes a cabin by the tower, which suggests an earlier building. Not resolved.

NHLR's January 2018 visit called the tower easily accessible. The Explorer says the landowner closed the property in 2018. Both can hold if the closure came after January 2018, but the sources give no month.

sources.title: A short jaunt with a fire tower outside Caroga Lake, and the hardest part is getting there

notes_for_editor: The brief had no build year; 1925 is added with the 1926 operating-year conflict noted. Access is marked restricted because a 2018 landowner closure is reported in the Explorer, but the Explorer piece is undated in the cache and no source says whether climbing the tower is permitted. The Explorer author climbed the tower; do not encourage climbing. The full NRHP nomination was not retrieved; the NPGallery listing had only metadata. The only NHLR visit is January 2018, so current condition is unknown. The NHLR page and the Wikipedia page are the sources for the staffing and build facts. Revised on fact-check 2026-10-08: 'covered in graffiti' now follows the Explorer's 'canvas for graffiti'; the 2021 DEC role in the roof and porch work is stated; the Explorer author still reached the tower after the 2018 closure report, which the story notes; the climbing sentence now cites all three sources it refers to.
